title: Hello, print()
learning_objectives: Run a Python program that prints text
Write string literals with single and double quotes
Control print's separator and line ending with sep and end
hints: `print("Python", "is", "fun")` already puts one space between the words.
`print()` with no arguments prints an empty line; `sep="-"` changes the separator.

failure_feedback.advice: Compare your output with the six expected lines; look for extra spaces or missing lines.
Use one print with three arguments; print adds the spaces for you.
Pass `sep="-"` so the parts are joined by dashes, not spaces.
Line 4 must be empty: call `print()` with no arguments.
The first call needs `end="..."` so `done` continues the same line.
Wrap the last string in single quotes so it can contain double quotes.
